body_es:
En Domain-Driven Design (DDD), un contexto delimitado (Bounded Context) es la frontera explícita dentro de la cual un modelo de dominio es coherente y consistente. Dentro del límite, los términos tienen un significado preciso. Fuera del límite, el mismo término puede significar algo diferente.

El ejemplo clásico es el concepto de "cliente": en el contexto de ventas, un cliente tiene un historial de pedidos y un límite de crédito; en el contexto de soporte técnico, un cliente tiene tickets abiertos y un nivel de servicio; en el contexto de facturación, un cliente tiene facturas y métodos de pago. Si los tres contextos comparten un único modelo de cliente, el código se vuelve complejo y frágil. Si cada contexto define su propio modelo, cada uno es simple y cohesivo.

Los contextos delimitados se comunican a través de interfaces bien definidas llamadas context maps. Los patrones de relación entre contextos incluyen: shared kernel (un submodelo compartido), customer-supplier (el proveedor define la API, el cliente se adapta), conformist (el consumidor adopta el modelo del proveedor sin modificarlo), y anti-corruption layer (el consumidor traduce el modelo del proveedor a su propio idioma).

Los bounded contexts son el fundamento para decidir los límites de los microservicios.
body_en:
In Domain-Driven Design (DDD), a Bounded Context is the explicit boundary within which a domain model is consistent and unambiguous. Inside the boundary, every term has a precise meaning. Outside it, the same term may mean something different.

The classic example is "Customer": in the Sales context, a customer has orders and a credit limit; in the Support context, a customer has open tickets and a service tier; in the Billing context, a customer has invoices and payment methods. A single shared Customer model that tries to serve all three contexts becomes large, coupled, and fragile. Separate, small models in each context keep each one simple and cohesive.

Bounded contexts communicate through well-defined interfaces captured in a Context Map. Relationship patterns include: Shared Kernel (a small shared sub-model owned jointly), Customer-Supplier (upstream provides an API the downstream adapts to), Conformist (downstream adopts the upstream model as-is), and Anti-Corruption Layer (downstream translates the upstream model into its own language to protect its internal purity).

Bounded contexts are the primary lens for deciding microservice boundaries in modern architectures.
example_code:
# Each bounded context defines its own Customer model
class SalesCustomer:
    """Customer in the Sales bounded context."""
    def __init__(self, customer_id, name, credit_limit):
        self.customer_id = customer_id
        self.name = name
        self.credit_limit = credit_limit
        self.orders = []

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'SalesCustomer({self.customer_id}, credit={self.credit_limit})'

class SupportCustomer:
    """Customer in the Support bounded context."""
    def __init__(self, customer_id, name, service_tier):
        self.customer_id = customer_id
        self.name = name
        self.service_tier = service_tier   # 'gold', 'silver', 'bronze'
        self.open_tickets = []

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'SupportCustomer({self.customer_id}, tier={self.service_tier})'

class BillingCustomer:
    """Customer in the Billing bounded context."""
    def __init__(self, customer_id, name, payment_method):
        self.customer_id = customer_id
        self.name = name
        self.payment_method = payment_method
        self.invoices = []

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'BillingCustomer({self.customer_id}, pay={self.payment_method})'

cid = 'C-001'
print(SalesCustomer(cid, 'Acme Corp', credit_limit=50000))
print(SupportCustomer(cid, 'Acme Corp', service_tier='gold'))
print(BillingCustomer(cid, 'Acme Corp', payment_method='wire-transfer'))
print('Each context owns its own model — no shared mutable state')
example_output:
SalesCustomer(C-001, credit=50000)
SupportCustomer(C-001, tier=gold)
BillingCustomer(C-001, pay=wire-transfer)
Each context owns its own model — no shared mutable state
source: Evans, E. — Domain-Driven Design (Addison-Wesley, 2003) ch. 14 — https://www.domainlanguage.com/ddd/
